brief: Ian asked for a review of Digital Garden plugin settings + the vault for accessibility wins. Research turned up one plugin setting worth enabling, three confirmed bugs, and one feature worth building — Ian confirmed all four.
fixed: Keyboard-inaccessible search trigger: searchButton.njk was a bare <div onclick> with no tabindex/role/aria-label — confirmed via live keyboard testing that Tab skipped it entirely inside the new menu panel. Changed to a real <button type="button"> with aria-label="Search"; native keyboard operability, zero JS needed. This is a shared component used site-wide, not menu-specific, so the fix applies everywhere it's used, including production's current inline nav.

Missing skip-to-content link: zero matches anywhere on the site (confirmed by grep). Added a components/skipLink.njk partial, included as the first focusable element in index.njk/note.njk/page.njk, targeting a new id="main-content" on each layout's <main>. Visually hidden via transform (not clipped off-screen), appears on :focus. Matters more now that a MENU button/panel sits before main content on every page.
Search input/results had no screen-reader semantics: added aria-label to #term and role="status" aria-live="polite" to #search-results so screen readers get search-state announcements.
built: Text-size control (A-/A/A+) in the menu's Preferences column, matching the feature wiobyrne.com's own menu already has (Header.astro) but the Digital Garden plugin itself does not expose to visitors. Uses %-based root font-size (90/100/115%) rather than fixed px, so it scales relative to whatever browser-level size preference the visitor already has rather than overriding it. Persisted via localStorage. Verified: no horizontal overflow even at the largest scale, since the site's spacing/type system is rem-based throughout.
vaultChange: Enabled dgShowToc in .obsidian/plugins/digitalgarden/data.json defaultNoteSettings (was false) — a genuine plugin-native heading-based table of contents, useful for keyboard/screen-reader navigation of long newsletter issues. This only affects future publishes; existing published notes need a republish from Obsidian to pick up the new default. Not something this session can trigger — flagged for Ian.

keyboard: Skip-link is the first tab stop on every page, activates and jumps to #main-content
Search button is now reachable via Tab (4th stop inside the open menu: Newsletter -> Subscribe -> Explore -> Search) and activates via Enter, opening the real search overlay
Text-size buttons sync aria-pressed correctly and persist across reload

brief: Ian's read on the first commit: panel felt cluttered/messy, like a first draft. Reworked panel content, not the toggle mechanism.
findings: 3 columns with 2/1/2 item weights left 'Explore' looking sparse and 'Preferences' unbalanced against 'Read'.
The relocated search control showed only a bare icon (its .search-text is display:none by default site-wide) — no label, unlike every other row, and floated with a large gap above the theme toggle.
Inconsistent row rhythm: Read/Subscribe links used one height+gap system, the Preferences controls used a different flex-column gap — nothing lined up.
fixed: Merged Read + Explore into one 'Navigate' column (Newsletter, Subscribe, Explore the garden) — 3 balanced items against Preferences' 2, no more single-item column.

Every row (links and controls) now shares one rule: min-height 2.4rem, hairline top rule, last-child gets a matching bottom rule — reads as one consistent list down each column instead of two different systems glued together.

Search control now shows its icon + 'Search' label (the same leading-icon + label pattern the Dark toggle already used), with the Ctrl+K keys badge hidden for parity — previously an inconsistent bare icon.

validation.keyboard: pass — Escape/outside-click/focus-return/tab-order all re-verified after the markup change

brief: Add a MENU toggle + overlay panel, adapting the shared Apparatus pattern from wiobyrne-astro's Header.astro. Branch design/dl-menu-panel, off current production main (independent of the still-open Grenze identity PR #15).
nav: N9-family closed state (wordmark + single MENU trigger, no inline links) expanding into a 3-column overlay panel: Read (Newsletter, Subscribe), Explore (Explore the garden — placeholder for Groves/Forests until those collections are populated), Preferences (search, light/dark toggle)
diversification: Replaces the previous N9 utility bar (wordmark + 4 inline items). Same closed-state minimalism, new expand-on-demand mechanism.
decisions: Panel is position:absolute overlay, not in-flow — avoids animating a layout property (max-height) to satisfy the motion discipline; only opacity + transform animate, panel visibility otherwise toggled via aria-hidden + inert.

Reused existing components as-is: searchButton.njk (plugin-managed onclick handler) and the .garden-theme-toggle button (its bootstrap script in 001-garden-theme.njk uses querySelector, unaffected by relocation into the panel).
'Explore the garden' link points to the existing /start-here/ route and reuses the homepage's own copy for the same concept — no fabricated /groves/ or /forests/ route invented.

Fixed a visual artifact during build/test: the homepage's absolutely-positioned hero-grove illustration poked out below the panel's bottom edge when open. Hidden via opacity while the menu is open (aria-hidden decorative element, zero information loss).

validation.darkMode: pass (verified via the real toggle interaction, not a class hack)
validation.keyboard: pass — Escape closes + returns focus to toggle; outside-click closes; Tab reaches panel content only when open (inert blocks it when closed); focus-visible ring confirmed in both themes
validation.searchIntegration: pass — clicking the relocated search button still opens the plugin's search overlay (.search-container gains .active) and auto-closes the menu panel

brief: Digitally Literate newsletter and curated public notebook
decisions: Public note types are Evergreen, Grove, and Forest.
Seed, Sprout, and Plant remain private development states.
Light mode is the default reading surface; explicit reader choice persists.
Texture is limited to semantic Apparatus regmarks, never resting-state backgrounds or body text.
Homepage rhythm uses a compact named spacing scale and avoids inherited plugin block margins.
Homepage illustration is a decorative grove, not a maturity-stage taxonomy mark.
The masthead retains the full Digitally Literate name.
The homepage title remains on one line while the earlier geometric grove form supplies the counterweight.
Evergreen motion is isolated to the tree forms; the grove baseline remains fixed.
